_comment: DOCUMENTATION ONLY -- DO NOT APPLY THIS FILE.
This records what the ECS TASK role (liftoff-api-task) should be able to do,
which is nothing. Create the role with task-role-trust-policy.json and attach
NO permissions policy at all.
An empty statement list is not a valid policy, and AWS says so:
aws accessanalyzer validate-policy --policy-type IDENTITY_POLICY ...
-> ERROR MISSING_STATEMENT: Add a statement to the policy.
That rejection is the confirmation -- 'no permissions' means no attachment,
not an empty one.
Why nothing:
The API makes no AWS API calls: its only outbound dependency is Supabase over
HTTPS, and those credentials arrive as environment variables injected by the
execution role before startup. So the running process needs nothing from AWS.
The role still has to exist, because ECS resolves taskRoleArn at task launch.
Create it with this trust policy and no permissions policy attached.
Do not be tempted to give it the execution role's SSM permissions 'to be safe'.
That would let application code -- or anything that compromises it -- read the
service-role Supabase key directly, which bypasses RLS entirely. The whole
point of the split is that the agent can read secrets and the app cannot.
If a future feature needs S3 or SES, add a narrowly scoped statement HERE, not
to the execution role.
